design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What type of search finds content based on meaning even when the exact words differ?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is hybrid search in database querying?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: A search approach that runs full-text search and vector search together and merges the results.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What trade-offs are important when choosing between full-text search, vector search, and hybrid search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Precision, recall, and performance.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which function can be used to write vector search queries in SQL?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What must be stored in a SQL database to prepare for vector search?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What technique combines ranked results from full-text and vector search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which search approach in SQL Server and Azure SQL Database is best for finding exact words and phrases in text data?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Full-text search. It matches terms in the query and understands language variations such as inflections.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which search approach finds results based on meaning rather than matching the exact query words?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Semantic vector search. It compares embeddings to find conceptually similar content even when different words are used.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What does hybrid search do in SQL Server and Azure SQL Database?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: It runs both full-text search and vector search, then combines the results. This helps when users may search by exact terms or by meaning.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: When is full-text search usually the better choice than vector search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: When the application needs exact matches or users know the specific words they want. Full-text search tends to return fewer, more precise results.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What data is required for vector search in SQL Server and Azure SQL Database?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Embeddings stored in vector columns. Vector search works over those embedding representations rather than over a full-text index.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) used for?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: RRF combines ranked results from multiple search methods into one list. It rewards documents that appear high in more than one result set.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What formula does Reciprocal Rank Fusion use to score a result?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: It uses `1/(rank + k)`, where `k` is 60. The final score is the sum of the scores from each result set.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Why can a document that is not ranked first in either full-text or vector search still rank highly in hybrid search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Because RRF adds the scores from multiple result lists. A document that appears in both lists can outrank a result that appears in only one list.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is the main advantage of full-text search over the SQL LIKE operator?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Full-text search understands words, phrases, and language rules, while LIKE only matches character patterns.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What two things are required to query full-text search in SQL Server?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: A full-text index on the text columns and full-text predicates in the WHERE clause.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which full-text predicate is used for exact matches of words and phrases?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which search approach is more appropriate when users search for concepts instead of specific words?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Vector search.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which vector distance metric measures the angle between vectors and ignores magnitude?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which function should you use for exact nearest neighbor vector search in SQL Server?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: `VECTOR_DISTANCE`. It compares the query vector against every vector in the table.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which function should you use for approximate nearest neighbor search when a vector index exists?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: `VECTOR_SEARCH`. It uses the vector index instead of scanning every row.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What vector index algorithm does SQL Server use for approximate nearest neighbor search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: DiskANN.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which function calculates the distance between two vectors using a specified metric and performs exact nearest-neighbor search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: VECTOR_DISTANCE. It computes the distance to every qualifying row.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which metrics are supported by VECTOR_DISTANCE?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: 'cosine', 'euclidean', and 'dot'.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What does VECTOR_SEARCH use to find nearest neighbors quickly on large tables?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: A vector index. It performs approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What column does VECTOR_SEARCH add to its result set?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: A distance column.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: When does VECTOR_SEARCH fall back to exact search?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: When no matching vector index exists for the target column and metric. It also raises a warning.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is the key caveat when filtering VECTOR_SEARCH results with a WHERE clause?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: The WHERE clause is applied after nearest neighbors are found, not before. This can filter out all of the top candidates.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Why would you request more candidates than needed from VECTOR_SEARCH before applying a filter?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: To compensate for post-filtering. It increases the chance that enough matching rows remain after the filter.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which function scales a vector to unit length?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is hybrid search in SQL used for?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which vector search functions can be used in a hybrid search pattern?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) used for?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: It combines ranked result lists from different sources into one score. It uses rank positions instead of raw scores.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Why is RRF often preferred over combining raw search scores?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: Because different search methods use different score scales, such as BM25 and cosine distance. RRF avoids score normalization by using ranks.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: What does the RRF constant `k` do?
design-implement-intelligent-search-with.A: It prevents very high-ranked items from dominating the combined score. A typical value is 60.

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Why is `FULL OUTER JOIN` used when merging hybrid search results?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: When should `VECTOR_SEARCH` be preferred over `VECTOR_DISTANCE`?

design-implement-intelligent-search-with.Q: Which search technique uses full-text indexes in Azure SQL Database to search text data?

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What problem does Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) solve for large language models?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It gives the model access to relevant external data at query time, so responses can be grounded in current information the model did not learn during training.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: In a RAG workflow, what is the role of retrieval before generating a response?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: Relevant data is fetched from a database or other source and added to the prompt so the model can answer using that context.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Why keep RAG processing inside the database layer?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It avoids moving data between systems and lets SQL control which context the model receives.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What kind of response should RAG help produce?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: A response grounded in actual, up-to-date information from the underlying data source.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What is one advantage of building the retrieval step in SQL rather than a separate service?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: The retrieval step stays close to the data, which simplifies the architecture and reduces data movement.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: When is RAG the right approach for an application?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: When the application needs the model to answer using specific, current data from your own systems rather than only the model's training data.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Why might SQL query results be converted to JSON for LLM processing?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: JSON provides a format that can be passed into a prompt for the model to use as context.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What is the purpose of combining instructions with database context in a prompt?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It tells the model what to do and supplies the relevant data needed to generate the answer.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What role do LLM endpoints play in an SQL-based RAG workflow?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: SQL can call the LLM endpoint to generate a response after the relevant data has been retrieved and prepared.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does RAG stand for in AI applications?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: Retrieval Augmented Generation. It combines retrieved data with a prompt so a model can generate a grounded answer.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What are the three main steps in a RAG workflow?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: Retrieve relevant data, augment the prompt with that data, and generate a response grounded in the retrieved context.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: How does RAG differ from fine-tuning?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: RAG keeps knowledge in your data store and supplies only the needed context at query time. Fine-tuning retrains the model so the knowledge is baked into the model itself.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: When is RAG a better choice than fine-tuning for changing data?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: When the underlying data changes frequently, such as inventory or product information. RAG can retrieve current data on each request.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Why is RAG useful for privacy-sensitive data?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It keeps data in your database and sends only the context needed for each request. Fine-tuning sends data to the model provider for training.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What role does SQL play in a RAG architecture?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: SQL stores the data, performs retrieval with full-text, vector, or hybrid search, and orchestrates prompt construction and model calls. The model runs externally.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Which stored procedure is used in SQL to call an external LLM endpoint in a RAG flow?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What kind of answers does RAG aim to produce?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: Grounded responses based on your retrieved data rather than the model's training data.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Why is JSON useful when passing SQL query results to a language model in a RAG workflow?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: A language model processes text, not relational structures, and JSON preserves field names and relationships in text form. That gives the model structured context it can use correctly.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does `FOR JSON AUTO` do in SQL Server or Fabric T-SQL?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It formats query results as JSON based on the query structure. Column names automatically become field names.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What is the main difference between `FOR JSON AUTO` and `FOR JSON PATH`?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: `FOR JSON AUTO` infers the JSON shape from the query, while `FOR JSON PATH` lets you explicitly control field names and nesting with column aliases.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: When should `WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER` be used with `FOR JSON`?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: Use it when returning a single record and you do not want the JSON array brackets. It is often useful for one customer, one product, or one order.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does `INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES` do in a `FOR JSON` query?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It keeps null fields in the JSON output instead of omitting them. Use it when the absence of a value is meaningful.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does `ROOT('name')` do in a `FOR JSON` query?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It wraps the entire JSON output in a named root element. This can help indicate what kind of data is being returned.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Why should you avoid including unnecessary columns such as internal IDs and audit timestamps in RAG context?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: They add noise and consume tokens without helping the model answer the question. Lean context usually improves answer quality and reduces token cost.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: In a RAG workflow, what is the purpose of `VECTOR_DISTANCE` after generating an embedding for the user question?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It finds the closest matching rows by comparing vectors. That helps retrieve relevant context before formatting it as JSON.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: In a chat prompt, which role sets the rules for how the assistant should behave?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: The system role.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: In a chat prompt, which role typically contains the user's question and the retrieved context?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: The user role.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does grounding mean in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: It means instructing the model to use your retrieved data as the source of truth rather than relying on general training data.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: Which T-SQL functions can be used to build JSON prompt payloads directly in the database?
design-implement-rag-with-sql.A: JSON_OBJECT and JSON_ARRAY.

design-implement-rag-with-sql.Q: What does the temperature parameter control in a language model request?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is one advantage of using proper constraints such as primary keys, foreign keys, and CHECK constraints?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which Azure SQL Database service tier automatically scales compute down to zero when idle and charges only for storage during inactive periods?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What capability does the Azure SQL Database Hyperscale tier provide for read-intensive workloads?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does Azure SQL Managed Instance provide in terms of SQL Server compatibility?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which Azure SQL Managed Instance feature supports near real-time synchronization from SQL Server to Azure for hybrid scenarios and minimal-downtime migrations?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which SQL Server features are available at the instance level in Azure SQL Managed Instance?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines let you control that PaaS offerings do not?
design-implement-database-objects.A: You control the SQL Server instance, database engine configuration, and the underlying Windows or Linux operating system. This provides maximum compatibility and customization.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does the SQL IaaS Agent extension add to SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is SQL database in Microsoft Fabric built on?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does automatic mirroring do in SQL database in Microsoft Fabric?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the SQL analytics endpoint in Microsoft Fabric?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which SQL data type is best for exact financial values that require precision, instead of approximate storage?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which string data type should you use for variable-length text in SQL Server?

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main purpose of a fact table in multidimensional analytics?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It stores measurable events or metrics. Dimension tables provide the context for analyzing those facts.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Why is DATETIME2 generally preferred over legacy DATETIME?
design-implement-database-objects.A: DATETIME2 provides better precision. It is a more modern date/time type for timestamp data.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main reason to choose NVARCHAR instead of VARCHAR?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Use NVARCHAR when you need Unicode support for international text. VARCHAR is more storage-efficient for ASCII-only data.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What type of primary key is typically smaller and more storage-efficient than a GUID-based key for a table like Product?
design-implement-database-objects.A: An INT IDENTITY key. It uses less storage and clusters efficiently.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main effect of using FLOAT for financial data instead of DECIMAL?
design-implement-database-objects.A: FLOAT can introduce rounding errors. Those errors can affect dependent calculations.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which SQL constructs help enforce data quality at the database level by preventing missing values and invalid relationships?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Constraints such as NOT NULL and foreign keys. They enforce rules directly in the table design.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main purpose of an index in a database?
design-implement-database-objects.A: To accelerate data retrieval by creating optimized lookup paths to table rows.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which type of index stores data in row format and is best for transactional workloads?
design-implement-database-objects.A: A rowstore index.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the key difference between a clustered index and a nonclustered index?
design-implement-database-objects.A: A clustered index determines the physical order of data rows in the table, while a nonclustered index has a separate structure that points to the rows.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: How many clustered indexes can a table have?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Only one.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: How many nonclustered indexes can a table have?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Multiple nonclustered indexes can be created on a table or indexed view.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: When are clustered indexes generally the best choice?
design-implement-database-objects.A: They are best for efficient range queries and ordered access patterns, such as identity or date-based sorting.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: When are nonclustered indexes generally the best choice?
design-implement-database-objects.A: They are best for fast lookups on specific predicates, joins, or sort patterns that do not match the clustered key.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main storage pattern used by a columnstore index?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It stores data column-by-column instead of row-by-row.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the maximum number of rows in a columnstore rowgroup?
Which SQL Server table type keeps data entirely in RAM to reduce disk I/O latency for high-throughput workloads?
design-implement-database-objects.A: In-memory optimized tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What option is used to create an in-memory optimized table in SQL Server?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Use `MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON` in the `CREATE TABLE` statement.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What SQL Server feature automatically tracks the full history of row changes for point-in-time queries?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Temporal tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which option enables system versioning for a temporal table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Use `SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON`.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What type of table lets you query data in external storage without importing it into SQL Server?
design-implement-database-objects.A: External tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What SQL Server table type provides tamper-evident records with cryptographic verification for auditing and compliance?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Ledger tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which two ledger table types are available in SQL Server?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Updatable ledger tables and append-only ledger tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What SQL Server table type is designed to model entities and relationships for traversing highly connected data?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Graph tables.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does a primary key constraint guarantee in a table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It guarantees unique rows and enforces entity integrity. The Database Engine also creates a unique index for the primary key columns.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the main purpose of a foreign key constraint?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It enforces referential integrity by ensuring that values in the foreign key table match valid rows in the referenced primary key table.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the difference between a PRIMARY KEY constraint and a UNIQUE constraint regarding NULL values?
design-implement-database-objects.A: A PRIMARY KEY column cannot contain NULL values. A UNIQUE constraint allows NULL, but only one NULL value per constrained column.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does a CHECK constraint enforce?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It enforces domain integrity by limiting the values accepted by one or more columns using a logical expression.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does a DEFAULT constraint do?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It supplies a default value when no value is provided during an INSERT operation.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: When should a sequence object be preferred over an identity column?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Use a sequence when you need a number before inserting, need to share one number series across tables or columns, or need to restart or reserve ranges of numbers.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Are sequence values automatically unique when inserted into a table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: No. Sequence values are not automatically protected or unique after insertion, so a unique constraint is needed if uniqueness is required.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Do sequence numbers get consumed if a transaction rolls back?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Yes. Sequence numbers are generated outside the current transaction and are consumed even if the transaction is rolled back.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: When are JSON columns a better fit than regular relational columns?
design-implement-database-objects.A: When the data is semi-structured and varies by row. They let you keep predictable fields in typed columns while storing variable fields in JSON.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which SQL function extracts a single scalar value from a JSON document?
design-implement-database-objects.A: JSON_VALUE.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Which SQL function returns a JSON object or array from a JSON document?
design-implement-database-objects.A: JSON_QUERY.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is one advantage of SQL Server 2025 native JSON storage over storing JSON as NVARCHAR(MAX)?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It stores JSON in a binary format optimized for querying and manipulation. It also supports more efficient reads, writes, and better compression.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: How do you update a single property in a native JSON column in SQL Server 2025+?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Use the modify method on the JSON value. It can change one property without rewriting the whole document.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Why is a computed column often used when indexing JSON data?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Because the JSON type itself cannot be used as an index key column. A computed column can extract a JSON property and be indexed instead.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What constraint function can you use to ensure a required JSON property exists?
design-implement-database-objects.A: JSON_PATH_EXISTS. It can be used in a CHECK constraint to validate required fields.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: In a mixed relational and JSON design, which data should remain in regular columns?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Predictable data with the same fields and consistent data types. JSON should be reserved for the variable parts.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What does table partitioning do to a large table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It divides the table into smaller physical partitions while keeping it as one logical table.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the partition function in SQL Server partitioning?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It defines how data is divided into partitions by specifying the boundary values or ranges.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is the purpose of a partition scheme?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It maps partitions to filegroups.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: When does partitioning usually improve query performance?
design-implement-database-objects.A: When most queries filter on the partition key, allowing partition elimination to access only relevant partitions.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is aligned indexing in a partitioned table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: An aligned index uses the same partition scheme as the base table, so each index partition matches a table partition.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is a key operational advantage of aligned indexes?
design-implement-database-objects.A: They enable fast partition switching for archival and simplify independent maintenance of partitions.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: Why is range partitioning commonly used?
design-implement-database-objects.A: It divides data into value ranges and works especially well for time-series, sequential, and numeric range data.

design-implement-database-objects.Q: What is a common best practice for the partition key in a partitioned table?
design-implement-database-objects.A: Choose a stable column that appears in the WHERE clause of most queries and include it in the primary key.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is a virtual table used to simplify data access and provide a security boundary?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A view.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is a precompiled T-SQL code block typically used for complex operations and data modifications?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A stored procedure.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is used for reusable calculations that return a single value?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A scalar function.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object returns a result set that can be used in queries?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A table-valued function.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object automatically responds to data modifications or database events?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A trigger.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is one benefit of using SQL Server programmability objects in a database application?
implement-programmability-objects.A: They help centralize logic and improve maintainability.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What kind of issue can triggers help address in a database?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Automatic validation and logging of data modifications.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why are views often used across multiple applications?
implement-programmability-objects.A: They reduce repeated JOIN logic and simplify data access.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is a view in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A virtual table based on a SELECT statement. It does not store data itself and returns data from underlying tables when queried.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is one common use of a SQL Server view for application code?
implement-programmability-objects.A: To hide complex joins, calculations, and filters behind a single query object. This makes application code simpler and easier to maintain.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How can a view help with security in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It can expose only specific columns or rows while restricting access to the underlying tables. This lets you grant limited access without giving full table access.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which statement is used to create a view in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: CREATE VIEW. It is followed by a SELECT query that defines the view.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does the WITH CHECK OPTION clause do in a view?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It forces INSERT and UPDATE operations through the view to match the view's WHERE condition. Rows that would not be visible in the view are rejected.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why should you specify column names explicitly instead of using SELECT * in a view?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Explicit column names make the view more maintainable and avoid unexpected changes when the underlying tables change. They keep the view definition stable.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: When is a view a good choice instead of a stored procedure?
implement-programmability-objects.A: When you want to encapsulate reusable query logic without parameters and present data in a simplified way. Stored procedures are better for data modification logic.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: When is an indexed view preferable to a regular view?
implement-programmability-objects.A: When performance-critical queries always return the same results and you want the result set stored physically. Indexed views are also called materialized views.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is a stored procedure in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A compiled collection of T-SQL statements that SQL Server stores and executes as a single unit.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why do stored procedures often run faster than ad hoc queries on repeated executions?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Their execution plans are cached after the first run, reducing parsing and optimization overhead.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL statement is used to create a stored procedure?
implement-programmability-objects.A: CREATE PROCEDURE.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does `SET NOCOUNT ON` do inside a stored procedure?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It prevents the message about the number of rows affected from being sent to the client, reducing network traffic.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How are input parameters defined in a stored procedure?
implement-programmability-objects.A: With the `@` symbol followed by a parameter name and data type.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How do you make a stored procedure parameter optional?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Assign it a default value, such as `= NULL`.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How are output parameters declared in a stored procedure?
implement-programmability-objects.A: By using the `OUTPUT` keyword in the parameter definition.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What must you do when calling a stored procedure that returns an output parameter?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Declare a variable to receive the value and use the `OUTPUT` keyword in the `EXECUTE` statement.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which T-SQL construct is used for stored procedure error handling?
implement-programmability-objects.A: `TRY...CATCH` blocks.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why should you check `@@TRANCOUNT` before rolling back in a `CATCH` block?
implement-programmability-objects.A: To avoid errors if the transaction already completed or was never started.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why should stored procedures use schema-qualified object names?
implement-programmability-objects.A: They remove ambiguity and improve performance by avoiding schema resolution overhead.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why should you avoid using `SELECT *` in production stored procedures?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Explicit columns are safer when table structures change and usually improve query performance.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does a scalar function return?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A single value of a specified data type.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which T-SQL statement is used to create a scalar function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: CREATE FUNCTION.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which clause in a scalar function definition specifies the return data type?
implement-programmability-objects.A: The RETURNS clause.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Can a scalar function be used directly in a SELECT statement or WHERE clause?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Yes. Scalar functions can be embedded directly in T-SQL expressions such as SELECT lists and WHERE clauses.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What statement is used to change an existing scalar function without dropping it first?
implement-programmability-objects.A: ALTER FUNCTION.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What statement is used to remove a scalar function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: DROP FUNCTION.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why is a scalar function that uses GETDATE() non-deterministic?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Because the return value can change depending on the current date and time. The same input can produce different results at different times.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What type of function is recommended as an alternative when a scalar function in a WHERE clause causes performance issues on large tables?
implement-programmability-objects.A: An inline table-valued function.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does a table-valued function return in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A result set, exposed as a table.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is the key difference between an inline table-valued function and a multi-statement table-valued function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: An inline TVF contains a single SELECT statement, while a multi-statement TVF uses a BEGIN...END block and explicitly defines the returned table structure.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: When is an inline table-valued function usually the better choice?
implement-programmability-objects.A: For simple parameterized queries that need better performance.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: When is a multi-statement table-valued function usually necessary?
implement-programmability-objects.A: When you need procedural logic, multiple steps, or iterative construction of the result set.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Can table-valued functions be used in JOIN clauses and SELECT statements?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Yes. They can be used like tables or views in queries.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does the CROSS APPLY operator do with a table-valued function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It invokes the function for each row from the outer table, especially when passing column values as parameters.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How does SQL Server determine the returned table structure for an inline table-valued function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: SQL Server infers the structure from the SELECT statement.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: How do you define the returned table structure in a multi-statement table-valued function?
implement-programmability-objects.A: You explicitly declare the table variable with its columns and data types.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is a trigger in SQL Server?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A special stored procedure that automatically executes when a specified event occurs in a database. Triggers are often used to maintain data integrity, enforce business rules, and automate database operations.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What is the difference between a DML trigger and a DDL trigger?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A DML trigger responds to data changes such as INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. A DDL trigger responds to schema changes such as CREATE, ALTER, and DROP.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: When does an AFTER trigger execute?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It executes after the triggering data modification statement completes. The database first performs the change, then runs the trigger.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What does an INSTEAD OF trigger do?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It runs in place of the original INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement. It is commonly used for views that do not support direct modification or for custom business logic.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: What are the inserted and deleted pseudo-tables used for in DML triggers?
implement-programmability-objects.A: They contain copies of the affected rows. INSERT populates inserted, DELETE populates deleted, and UPDATE populates both.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which trigger function is used to test whether a specific column was modified by an UPDATE statement?
implement-programmability-objects.A: The UPDATE(column_name) function. It returns whether the specified column was targeted by the UPDATE statement.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why can combining multiple trigger actions into one trigger be useful?
implement-programmability-objects.A: It lets one trigger handle INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE when the same logic applies to multiple operations. This can reduce duplication and simplify maintenance.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Why should trigger logic usually be kept minimal and efficient?
implement-programmability-objects.A: Because triggers run during qualifying operations and can affect database performance and transaction throughput. Complex work is often better logged and processed asynchronously.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is the only one that can be used directly in a SELECT or JOIN clause and also accept parameters?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A function.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object can automatically execute in response to data modification events?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A trigger.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is best for executing complex business logic with multiple statements and transaction control?
implement-programmability-objects.A: A stored procedure.

implement-programmability-objects.Q: Which SQL Server programmability object is commonly used to simplify access to complex joins without accepting parameters?

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL feature is commonly used to organize complex queries and traverse hierarchical data?

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL feature is used for ranking, aggregation, and analytical calculations across row sets?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Window functions.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL feature is used to parse, construct, and transform JSON data?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON functions.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which technique is used for pattern matching, validation, and text manipulation in T-SQL?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Regular expressions.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL capability helps find approximate matches, such as similar names with misspellings?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Fuzzy string matching.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL feature uses the MATCH operator to traverse relationships?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Graph queries.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which type of query is used for row-by-row comparisons and calculations?

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL patterns are used to build reliable, production-ready code that responds gracefully to unexpected situations?

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL function family is used to parse, query, or modify JSON data in SQL Server?

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What type of T-SQL functions operate across a set of rows to calculate results such as running totals or rankings?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Window functions.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What T-SQL construct defines a temporary named result set that can be referenced within a single statement?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A Common Table Expression (CTE).

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What clause is used to define a Common Table Expression (CTE) in T-SQL?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: The WITH clause.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: How long does a CTE exist in SQL Server?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Only for the duration of the single statement that uses it. It does not persist as a table.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What are the two parts of a recursive CTE called?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: The anchor member and the recursive member.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What default recursion limit does SQL Server apply to recursive CTEs?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: 100 levels.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which query hint changes the recursion limit for a recursive CTE?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: OPTION (MAXRECURSION n).

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which DML statements can use a CTE in addition to SELECT?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What function is commonly used to prevent division by zero when calculating a value from CTE results?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: NULLIF.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What SQL operator combines the anchor and recursive members in a recursive CTE?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: UNION ALL.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does the `OVER` clause define in a SQL window function?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It defines the window of rows used for the calculation. It can include partitioning, ordering, and frame boundaries.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which clause divides rows into groups for a window function calculation?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `PARTITION BY`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is the main difference between a window function and a regular aggregate function?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A window function preserves individual rows in the result set. A regular aggregate function collapses rows into grouped output.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which ranking function assigns a unique sequential number to each row even when values are tied?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `ROW_NUMBER()`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which ranking function gives tied rows the same rank and leaves gaps in the հաջnext rank values?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `RANK()`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which ranking function gives tied rows the same rank without skipping the next rank number?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `DENSE_RANK()`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which function divides rows into a specified number of roughly equal groups?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `NTILE(n)`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does `LAG()` return?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It returns a value from a previous row in the ordered window. The offset and default value can be specified.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does `LAST_VALUE()` require to return the last row in the entire partition instead of the current row?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: An explicit frame that includes rows after the current row, such as `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL function extracts a scalar value from a JSON string?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON_VALUE(). It returns a scalar as NVARCHAR(4000).

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL function extracts a JSON object or array without removing its structure?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON_QUERY(). It returns objects and arrays as valid JSON strings.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does OPENJSON return by default when no schema is specified?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Three columns: key, value, and type.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which clause in OPENJSON maps JSON properties to typed columns?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: The WITH clause.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which join operator should be used instead of CROSS APPLY to keep rows that have NULL or empty JSON values?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: OUTER APPLY.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL Server 2022 function creates a JSON object from key-value pairs?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON_OBJECT().

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL Server 2022 function creates a JSON array from values?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON_ARRAY().

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which function aggregates multiple row values into a single JSON array?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: JSON_ARRAYAGG().

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which regex function returns 1 when a string matches a pattern and 0 when it does not?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_LIKE. It is typically used in WHERE clauses for validation and filtering.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function replaces all matches of a pattern with a specified string?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_REPLACE. It is commonly used for cleansing and standardizing text values.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function extracts the portion of a string that matches a pattern?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_SUBSTR. It can also return a capture group when requested.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function returns the starting position of a pattern match, and what does it return if no match is found?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_INSTR. It returns 0 if no match is found.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function returns how many times a pattern appears in a string?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_COUNT. It counts the number of matches in the input string.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function splits a string into rows based on a delimiter pattern?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE. It is a table-valued function that returns split values as rows.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL regular expression function returns all matches as separate rows?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: REGEXP_MATCHES. It is a table-valued function that outputs each match separately.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What regex syntax standard is used by SQL Server regular expression functions?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: ECMAScript regex syntax. This makes the patterns similar to those used in JavaScript and many other tools.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does edit distance measure between two strings?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It measures the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to transform one string into the other. Lower values mean the strings are more similar.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL function returns the Levenshtein distance between two strings?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `EDIT_DISTANCE`.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What output range does `EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY` use?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It returns a normalized similarity score from 0 to 100, where 100 means identical strings.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What output range does `JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE` use?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It returns a score from 0 to 1, where 1 means identical strings.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which fuzzy matching function is optimized for short strings such as person names?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE`. It gives higher scores to strings that match from the beginning.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which fuzzy matching function is often better for longer strings such as addresses or descriptions?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: `EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY`. It is often easier to use for longer strings than Jaro-Winkler.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Why should fuzzy matching usually be applied only after prefiltering a candidate set?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Because fuzzy matching is computationally expensive and must compare many characters in both strings. Prefiltering reduces the number of rows that need similarity calculations.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is a practical threshold indicator for Jaro-Winkler name matching?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A score above 0.9 typically indicates a strong match for names.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What SQL clause is used to create a node table in SQL graph?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Use the `AS NODE` clause in `CREATE TABLE`. SQL Server then adds a system-generated `$node_id` column.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What SQL clause is used to create an edge table in SQL graph?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Use the `AS EDGE` clause in `CREATE TABLE`. SQL Server automatically adds `$edge_id`, `$from_id`, and `$to_id` columns.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does the `$node_id` column represent in a node table?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It is the system-generated unique identifier for each node. SQL Server uses it internally for graph relationships.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What must you insert into an edge table to connect two nodes?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: You must supply the `$from_id` and `$to_id` values from the connected nodes. These should come from the nodes' `$node_id` values.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is the purpose of the `MATCH` clause in SQL graph queries?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It performs pattern matching across nodes and edges. This lets you express graph traversals directly instead of writing many joins.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: In a `MATCH` pattern, what does the arrow direction indicate?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It indicates the relationship direction. `(Node1)-(Edge)->(Node2)` means the edge goes from Node1 to Node2.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is the main use of `SHORTEST_PATH` in SQL graph queries?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It finds the shortest connection across a variable number of relationships. It is used for variable-length traversals.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: When should you prefer graph queries over relational queries?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Use graph queries when relationships are the primary focus or when you need variable-depth traversal. They are also useful for path-finding and connectivity analysis.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is a correlated subquery in SQL?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A subquery that references one or more columns from the outer query. It depends on each outer row and is evaluated once per row.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: How does a correlated subquery differ from a noncorrelated subquery in execution?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A noncorrelated subquery runs once and returns a fixed result. A correlated subquery runs repeatedly, once for each row processed by the outer query.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does the EXISTS operator return when used with a correlated subquery?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A Boolean-style result: true if at least one matching row exists, otherwise false. It does not return the matching data itself.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Why is EXISTS often more efficient than IN with a subquery?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: The database engine can stop searching after finding the first match with EXISTS. IN may need to evaluate all matching values.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is a common use of a correlated subquery in the SELECT clause?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: To calculate a separate value for each row, such as an average, count, or maximum from related rows. It lets you add contextual values without grouping the result set.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What must a correlated subquery in the SELECT clause return?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Exactly one value for each outer row. If multiple rows are possible, the subquery should be wrapped in an aggregate like MAX() or COUNT().

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: When is a window function usually preferred over a correlated subquery for row comparisons?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: For running totals, rankings, or previous/next row access. Functions like LAG() and LEAD() are typically more efficient and readable.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is the main performance risk of correlated subqueries on large tables?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: They can execute once per outer row, causing many repeated subquery evaluations. This can become very expensive on large datasets.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which T-SQL construct transfers execution from a TRY block to a CATCH block when an error occurs?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: A TRY...CATCH block. Errors raised in the TRY block are handled in the CATCH block.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Which SQL Server functions return the error number, message, severity, state, line number, and procedure name inside a CATCH block?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: ERROR_NUMBER(), ERROR_MESSAGE(), ERROR_SEVERITY(), ERROR_STATE(), ERROR_LINE(), and ERROR_PROCEDURE().

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: Why should @@TRANCOUNT be checked before calling ROLLBACK TRANSACTION in a CATCH block?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Because the transaction may already be rolled back or may never have started. Rolling back without an active transaction causes another error.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What custom error number range should be used for user-defined errors raised with THROW?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: 50000 or higher.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What does SET XACT_ABORT ON do in SQL Server?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: It makes SQL Server automatically roll back the transaction when an error occurs. This helps ensure consistent transactional behavior.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: When is RAISERROR preferred over THROW?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: Use RAISERROR when you need formatted messages with parameter substitution or compatibility with existing error-handling patterns.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What is the main difference between THROW and RAISERROR for new code?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: THROW is the recommended choice for new code because it is simpler and always includes a stack trace. RAISERROR is mainly used for formatting or legacy compatibility.

write-advanced-sql-code.Q: What should the outer procedure do when it owns a transaction and a nested stored procedure fails?
write-advanced-sql-code.A: The outer procedure should roll back the transaction if @@TRANCOUNT is greater than 0 and then rethrow the error. The inner procedure should not manage the rollback.
